data.title: India's Rising Inflation Strengthens Case for Rate Hikes — Market Talk
data.description:
0426 GMT - Faster price increases in India, driven by costs of food and oil and rising core inflation, strengthen the case for a shallow rate-hiking cycle, Nomura analysts Sonal Varma and Aurodeep Nandi say in a note. Consumer prices rose 4.8% on year in August from 4.5% in July, while core inflation accelerated to 4.2% from 3.9%. The bank now expects 50 bps of rate hikes in 4Q, with the Reserve Bank of India raising rates in October and December. Nomura has raised its fiscal 2027 inflation forecast to 5.1% from 4.6%, above the central bank's 5.0% projection.(venkat.pr@wsj.com)

0417 GMT - Treasury Secretary Bessent reiterated his support for the crypto Clarity Act ahead of a key Senate vote, calling the legislation "essential to ensuring America wins the global race for new technology." Bessent said on X that the act's final draft furthers the administration's mission of enabling digital technology while supporting community banks. That's been a point of contention, with critics worried that the legislation doesn't do enough to protect community banks from deposit flight caused by interest-like payments on stablecoin balances. Bessent said the draft gives the Treasury additional authority to safeguard community banks. "If stablecoins cause harm to community banks, I will not hesitate to use these tools to ensure they remain fully protected." The upcoming vote will decide if the act enters final voting procedures or gets pushed back. (fabiana.negrinochoa@wsj.com)

0353 GMT - BlackRock Investment Institute stays pro-risk even as global rates raise the hurdle for returns. Higher rates and strong equities can co-exist, strategists say. When higher yields reflect robust investment and growth, resulting earnings strength can help offset higher capital costs. Exceptional earnings growth, attractive valuations and a cleaner tactical backdrop support its U.S. and AI overweight positions, and a return to overweight in EM equities. However, BlackRock sees little room for complacency amid risks like renewed energy prices keeping inflation elevated just as the Fed faces a tough choice. A hold could test its credibility, with term premium acting as a release valve as investors demand more compensation to hold long-term bonds. That could push yields higher and raise the bar for equity returns. (fabiana.negrinochoa@wsj.com)

0333 GMT - The Singapore dollar weakens against its U.S. counterpart in the Asian session as gains in U.S. Treasury yields improve the appeal of U.S. dollar-denominated fixed-income assets. Overnight, the 10-year U.S. yield rose above 5% for the first time since 2023. Investors are cautious ahead of the Fed's interest rate decision later this week, Phillip Securities' research team says in a note. The Fed is widely expected to raise interest rates, they add. The U.S. dollar rises 0.1% to S$1.2716.(amanda.lee@wsj.com)

0332 GMT - China's new-home market is showing tentative signs of stabilization, but not a broad recovery, says Yuhan Zhang, principal economist at The Conference Board's China Center. The latest data show divergence even among major markets, with the secondhand housing sector considerably weaker than the new-home segment. The gap is economically important, says Zhang. New-home prices are stabilizing selectively, aided by policy measures, developer pricing strategies and stronger projects in core cities. Resale prices--which respond more directly to demand and sellers' willingness to cut prices--show underlying market confidence remains subdued. "We see some signs of stabilization in a few high-demand markets like Shanghai, but the nationwide picture is still not buyers bidding prices higher." (fabiana.negrinochoa@wsj.com)

0310 GMT - China's economy continues to show diverging signals, as consumption and investment remain weak, while industrial production powers on, says Zhiwei Zhang at Pinpoint Asset Management. Data earlier showed expected weakness in retail sales--a gauge of consumption--alongside continued contraction in investing activity and solid growth in factory output. Unemployment edged higher, while the property sector's struggles persist. After the economy slowed in 2Q, Zhang says the market is waiting for fiscal policy to become more supportive in 3Q. But there is so far no clear sign of stronger fiscal spending yet, he adds. That leaves China's economy open to downside risks as it will take time for fiscal support to be implemented and transmitted. (fabiana.negrinochoa@wsj.com)

0304 GMT - Indonesia's appointment of new finance minister Suahasil Nazara suggests fiscal prudence, policy continuity and confidence amid macroeconomic uncertainty, CIMB economists say in a note. His appointment is seen as timely, as the country is facing higher oil prices. Brent crude oil prices hovering around $110 per barrel increases Indonesia's fiscal and inflation risks. Recent natural disasters in the country could also weigh on economic growth and add to spending needs, they note. However, as Nazara is a seasoned fiscal technocrat and a familiar policy hand, his experience should support policy coordination and execution. This would help anchor market confidence while balancing growth and stability, they say.(amanda.lee@wsj.com)

0253 GMT - Global auto sales will likely decline by 4% this year due to weakness in China, Daiwa analyst Kelvin Lau writes in a note. Global auto sales will likely remain sluggish next year, with weakness persisting through 2029, he adds. An increasing number of automakers are using their current technology and capital to develop new segments such as humanoid robots to maintain long-term profitability, he adds. Among the automakers, Daiwa's top picks are BYD, Hyundai Motor and XPeng under the transformation theme. XPeng plans to ultimately sell part of its humanoid robot business in the coming 18 months, but remain a controlling shareholder. (jiahui.huang@wsj.com; @ivy_jiahuihuang)

0247 GMT - Taiwan central bank's September rate decision looks to be a close call. Four of seven economists polled by The Wall Street Journal expect the central bank to stand pat. Economists who expect the Central Bank of the Republic of China to stay on hold for a 10th consecutive quarter think a benign August inflation read suggests no urgency for a hike as the island economic growth remains robust. However, Deutsche Bank expects the CBC to raise rates by 12.5 bps at both in September and December, taking the policy rate to 2.25% by end-2026. ING economists, who call the situation "close to a coin flip," reckon that the Federal Reserve decision before the CBC meeting could affect things. (sherry.qin@wsj.com)

0224 GMT - Asian currencies mostly weaken in Asian trade, after the 10-year U.S. Treasury yield surged above 5% on Monday before settling at 4.960%. The rise in Treasury yield was driven by persistent inflation concerns, elevated oil prices, large government borrowing requirements, and heavy corporate issuance associated with artificial intelligence investment, Commerzbank Research analysts say in a note. The 5% level is psychologically and economically significant, they note, as sustained yields above the level would further tighten financial conditions. The U.S. dollar rises 0.3% to 154.82 yen and 0.45% higher at 1353.14 won, while the Australian dollar is 0.15% lower at US$0.7126, LSEG data show.(amanda.lee@wsj.com)

0221 GMT - Australian consumer spending rose 1.1% in August, which at face value looks healthy, but exclude rising fuel costs and the increase falls to a more moderate 0.6% rise, says CBA. Non-discretionary spending rose 2.2% in August driven by a sharp 12% rise in fuel outlays, the bank adds. Total discretionary spending growth slowed to 0.4%, it adds. The small increase follows a 12% in July. The data comes as Canberra is ruling out another short-term cut to fuel taxes to ease the burden of rising oil prices.(james.glynn@wsj.com; X @JamesGlynnWSJ)

0140 GMT - Standard Chartered says that it is finding it hard to go against market expectations for interest rate increases by the Federal Reserve. Steven Engander, co-head of FX Research at SC, says he can only imagine how hard it is for Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh to stare down the market. Yet there seems to have been a market echo chamber pushing up expectations despite a limited amount of incoming data, and little sign that inflation is going up, he adds. Some indicators suggest that underlying inflation is much lower if tariffs are removed, he adds. There is a very low cost to waiting, he says. (james.glynn@wsj.com; X @JamesGlynnWSJ)

data.title: IT stocks power Nifty's gap-up as crude, Fed weigh on outlook
data.description:
Markets opened higher on Tuesday, September 15, with the Nifty 50 rising 114.20 points (0.49 per cent) to 23,512.30 and the Sensex gaining 429.10 points (0.57 per cent) to 75,210.86 as of 9.17 am, reversing two sessions of consecutive losses.

The Sensex had closed the previous session at 74,781.76, opening today at 75,369.63, while the Nifty's previous close was 23,398.10, with an opening at 23,576.15.

Information technology stocks led the rebound, with all five top Nifty gainers drawn from the sector. HCL Technologies surged 5.21 per cent to ₹1,268.90 on the highest percentage gain of the session, while Infosys climbed 4.82 per cent to ₹1,087.70 on volumes of over 15 lakh shares valued at ₹16,499.52 lakhs.

Tech Mahindra added 4.61 per cent to ₹1,612.00, TCS rose 4.25 per cent to ₹2,294.30, and TMPV gained 4.80 per cent to ₹315.55.

On the losing side, Kotak Mahindra Bank fell 1.15 per cent to ₹414.20, BEL declined 1.08 per cent to ₹400.00, Grasim slipped 0.97 per cent to ₹3,250.00, Titan dropped 0.96 per cent to ₹4,961.50, and Hindalco lost 0.92 per cent to ₹972.50.

The recovery came despite a weak global backdrop. Wall Street closed lower overnight, with the Dow Jones shedding 0.29 per cent, the S&P 500 falling 0.48 per cent, and the Nasdaq dropping 0.56 per cent.

Selling in semiconductor and AI-related stocks, with Nvidia falling more than 2 per cent, dragged technology indices after concerns emerged over the pace of AI development. The U.S. 10-year Treasury yield briefly crossed 5 per cent for the first time since 2023, its highest level since that year.

Brent crude remains a primary concern, trading near $107 a barrel following Houthi attacks on Saudi oil infrastructure and clashes involving U.S. naval vessels and Iranian tankers in the region.

The Indian rupee fell 33 paise in the previous session to close at 94.82, hurt by aggressive dollar buying and elevated oil prices. As a net oil importer, India faces direct pressure on its import bill and inflation outlook from elevated energy costs.

..."Brent crude at $107 and the damage caused to the Saudi East-West oil pipeline from the Houthi attack will continue to weigh on markets,"... said Dr. V K Vijayakumar, Chief Investment Strategist, Geojit Investments. ..."This is a scenario which the Fed cannot ignore in the FOMC meeting tomorrow. Even though President Trump doesn't want a rate hike, his appointee Kevin Warsh is most likely to hike rates by 25 basis points because it would be difficult to justify a hold in rates in the present macro scenario."...

The U.S. Federal Reserve's two-day FOMC meeting begins today, with markets pricing a 60 per cent probability of a rate hike. A hawkish outcome could strengthen the dollar, pressure foreign inflows into Indian equities, and further weaken the rupee. ..."The September 15–16 FOMC meeting will remain the principal global trigger. A rate hike accompanied by hawkish guidance could strengthen the dollar and pressure global equities, foreign flows and the rupee,"... noted Hariselvan Radhakrishnan, Founder and CEO of HST Wealth.

Asian markets traded mixed, the Nikkei rose around 0.4 per cent and the Hang Seng gained 0.5 per cent, while the Kospi remained flat.

Domestic institutional investors (DIIs) have been providing a buffer against foreign selling. In the previous session on September 11, FIIs remained net sellers for the fourth consecutive session, offloading equities worth ₹930 crore, while DIIs purchased equities worth ₹1,968 crore.

Technically, the Nifty had been printing lower highs and lower bottoms and remains more than 1,050 points below its August swing high of 24,774. Analysts noted the index briefly touched an intraday low of 23,231 last Thursday before recovering. ..."The market has reached relatively oversold levels. While the short-term trend remains weak, the possibility of a quick pullback rally from current levels cannot be ruled out,"... said Shrikant Chouhan, Head of Equity Research at Kotak Securities, who placed immediate support for traders at 23,200 on the Nifty and 74,200 on the Sensex.

A positive from the domestic side: ..."There is clarity emerging on the choice of HDFC Bank MD and CEO. A quick acceptance of the name of the successor by the RBI can influence the benchmark index significantly,"... added Vijayakumar, pointing to the continuing boom in the IPO market and outperformance of the broader market as further positives.

Realty and IT were last week's biggest sectoral laggards, the Realty index fell 6.50 per cent and the IT index lost 5.75 per cent, though IT is staging a sharp recovery this morning.

Resistance for the Nifty is placed at 23,500–23,600, with analysts cautioning that a sustained move above 23,600 is necessary to confirm a recovery."Sustained trading above 24,000 would be required to improve the near-term technical setup and trigger a meaningful recovery,"... said Devarsh Vakil, Head of Prime Research at HDFC Securities.

data.title: New Hope's Forecast for Year Ahead: More of the Same — Interview
data.description:
By Rhiannon Hoyle

Australian coal producer New Hope expects steady output at its Bengalla mine and a continued ramp up of operations at New Acland over the coming year, as the company positions itself to capitalize on a tightening coal market driven by ongoing conflict in the Middle East, its chief executive officer said.

New Hope reported a 63% drop in annual net profit on Tuesday as the Bengalla mine recovered from severe weather disruptions, but doubled its final dividend as output and sales exceeded guidance. Shares were 4.1% higher in early afternoon trading in Sydney.

"Really more of the same," CEO Rob Bishop said in an interview when asked what investors should expect from the year ahead.

New Hope plans to issue fiscal 2027 annual guidance alongside its first-quarter production report in November, as it has done in the past.

Investors will "see consistent production from Bengalla, so that should just be a continuation," Bishop said. New Hope has been consistently operating that mine, located in Australia's New South Wales state, at its target 13.4 million metric ton run-of-mine production rate in recent months, he said.

At the New Acland operation in neighboring Queensland state, New Hope is ramping production toward a target of roughly 5 million tons a year of saleable coal.

The site produced 3.3 million tons in fiscal 2026, a 17% increase year over year. "You'll see that move into the fours for FY27," said Bishop. "And, as a result, you'll see cost of production reduce at Acland as we get more tonnage to spread the fixed cost of that mine."

New Hope will likely keep a buy-back program in place to purchase shares when the it thinks there's value in doing so, said Bishop. Although, a rally in the miner's stock this year means it has to date only spent a fraction--about 10%--of its 100 million Australian dollar pot, equivalent to US$71.4 million.

"We'll take advantage of that when the share price is lower," he said.

Fanning its shares has been a rise in the price of coal New Hope sells for power generation.

Bishop said the coal market is tightening as oil and gas supplies are disrupted amid the conflict in the Middle East. Saudi Arabia's East-West Pipeline was shut after multiple drone attacks last week.

"Essentially that impacts the whole energy complex," Bishop said. "Security of supply is paramount."

Over the long term, New Hope is expecting coal demand to ratchet up due to electrification and data centers for the artificial intelligence boom, he said.

"I think even the most modest forecasts on energy demand are very strong, and it's not the case that any one form of energy supply is going to cover that off," said Bishop.

Beyond the Bengalla and New Acland mines, New Hope has a 26% stake in closely held Malabar Resources, which is ramping up the Maxwell underground mine in New South Wales. That mine will mostly produce coal for steelmaking.

New Hope has raised its stake in that company in recent years, including as recently as a year ago. Bishop said he "gets asked a lot" about New Hope's plans for that investment.

"It's an exciting asset," he said. "But we understand our ability to underground mine is emerging, and we feel as through the shareholders there and the operators there are doing a great job."

Write to Rhiannon Hoyle at rhiannon.hoyle@wsj.com

data.title: Australia's Latrobe Magnesium surges after outlining US plant plans
data.description:
Australia's Latrobe Magnesium unveiled plans on Tuesday to build a magnesium plant in the U.S. with an estimated capital cost of $1.1 billion to $1.5 billion to tap into the North American market, sending its shares up 80% in intraday trade.

Here are some more details:

  • Shares of the Sydney-based company were last up 50% at 0420 GMT, heading for their biggest one-day gain in nearly five years.

  • The magnesium producer said the project will be the first commercial-scale magnesium-producing plant in North America, delivering for the U.S. defence, which faces a supply shortage.

  • The company said it aims to build a 50,000-metric-ton-per-annum (ktpa) plant, which can be expanded to 100 ktpa.

  • First production is targeted in 2030, the firm said.

data.title: China, HK stocks steady as AI hardware bounce counters weak data
data.description:
China and Hong Kong stocks held steady on Tuesday, as a mild rebound in AI hardware shares failed to offset losses elsewhere, with mixed August data pointing to persistently weak domestic demand.

** China's blue-chip CSI300 Index was flat by the lunch break, while the Shanghai Composite Index lost 0.1%. Hong Kong benchmark Hang Seng was down 0.2%.

** China's industrial output picked up pace in August, though sluggish consumption and a worsening investment slump reinforced concerns over deepening economic imbalances.

** Meanwhile, new home prices fell again in August, underscoring persistent weakness in the housing market.

** The CSI 300 Financial and Real Estate Index fell nearly 1% each, while consumer staple shares were flat.

** "Following weaker​-​than​-​expected credit demand, August activity data reinforced our view that a recovery in domestic demand remains elusive," Barclays analysts said in a note, adding that they maintain their below​-​consensus 2026 GDP growth forecast of 4.5%.

** The tech-focused STAR50 Index rose as much as 3%, rebounding for the first time in a week from a 4-1/2-month low. The CSI Semiconductor Material and Equipment Thematic Index (.CSI931743) gained 2.7%.

** Onshore sentiment has weakened over the past month, after investors took profits from a record-breaking AI-led rally earlier this year. Liquidity has also dried up. Daily turnover of onshore shares hovered near the lowest level since April over the past week.

** Tech majors listed in Hong Kong gained 0.8%, with Tencent up nearly 3%.

** Shares of Guangdong Tianyu Semiconductor jumped more than 8% on the company's share buyback plan.

data.title: Chicago wheat slips as Black Sea supply worries ease
data.description:
U.S. wheat futures fell on Tuesday, hovering near a more than two-week low, as hopes of reduced tensions in the Black Sea region eased supply concerns after Washington said Ukraine and Russia agreed not to target each other's energy infrastructure.

The most-active wheat contract on the Chicago Board of Trade (CBOT) was down 0.55% at $7.18 a bushel, as of 0410 GMT.

Traders continued to monitor risks to vital Black Sea grain export routes. Ukraine President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said on Monday that Kyiv was ready to support a U.S. proposal for a ceasefire on energy sites only if Washington could ensure Moscow was genuinely ready to end its war on Ukraine.

Soybeans lost 0.48% to $12.98 a bushel and corn dropped 0.33% to $5.31-1/2 a bushel.

The U.S. Department of Agriculture on Monday reported harvest progress at 8% for corn and 6% for soybeans, as of Sunday, ahead of their respective five-year averages of 6% and 3%.

However, the prospect of harvest delays in the Midwest offered some support to corn and soybean prices. Forecasts called for heavy rain across parts of the Midwest this week, potentially slowing fieldwork in Iowa, the largest U.S. corn-producing state and the second-largest soybean producer.

Traders were also optimistic about Chinese demand for U.S. soybeans ahead of Chinese President Xi Jinping's expected visit to Washington.

Commodity funds were net sellers of CBOT wheat and net buyers of soy, traders said on Monday. (CBOT/FUNDS)

data.title: ZAWYA: Saudi: WSP lands design contract for King Fahd International Airport
data.description:
By Staff Writer

Global engineering and professional services firm WSP has secured the design contract for the development of King Fahd International Airport in Dammam.

The project scope includes designing the expansion of passenger terminals, upgrading facilities, and improving airport entrances and access roads. It also includes developing baggage handling systems, digital services, and terminal wayfinding systems to streamline travel procedures and enhance passenger comfort, said Dammam Airports in a statement.

The master plan aims to serve more than 19.3 million passengers annually by 2030, with capacity to be increased in phases to 32 million passengers per year to meet future travel demand. It also targets increasing air cargo capacity to more than 600,000 tonnes annually and aircraft operational capacity to 77 movements per hour, supported by comprehensive expansions of infrastructure, runways, and general aviation facilities.

The agreement was signed by Dammam Airports CEO Eng. Mohammed Al Hassany and President of WSP for the Middle East and Asia Dean McGrail.

Speaking on the occasion, Al Hassany said signing the contract marks a significant milestone in the development of King Fahd International Airport.

He emphasized that Dammam Airports is committed to upgrading airport facilities, increasing capacity, and delivering a seamless, high-quality travel experience through modern design solutions and smart technologies that meet travelers' needs and accommodate future growth in passenger and air cargo traffic. This will reinforce the airport's status as an international gateway connecting Eastern Region to the world.

data.title: Advantage China in New Delhi's BRICS summit?
data.description:
By Ira Dugal

The annual BRICS summit in New Delhi was a diplomatic win for India, bringing together nations with divergent priorities and agendas. But did it also provide a platform for China to showcase its rising global influence? That's our focus this week.

Share your view on the key takeaways from the September 12 to 13 BRICS summit with me at ira.dugal@thomsonreuters.com.

And a further rise in inflation in August and a renewed surge in global oil prices clinch the case for India's first rate hike in nearly four years. Scroll down for more on that.

THIS WEEK IN ASIA

  • Trapped nine days in a dark tunnel, Nepali man tells his survival story

  • Houthis strike Saudi targets anew as talks over Strait of Hormuz stall

  • With yen surging, what will fund FX carry trades now?: McGeever​

  • 'Good move': Indonesia's finance minister switch will ease investor jitters

  • Supply squeeze in marine fuel eases as market adapts to prolonged Hormuz disruption

PHOTO OPS, SONGS AND A PROMISE OF COOPERATION

With photo opportunities, songs and a nearly 18,000-word joint communique, the summit of an expanded BRICS grouping appeared, at least on the surface, to be a success.

Chinese President Xi Jinping travelled to India for the first time in seven years, following a border conflict. Xi, Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Russian President Vladimir Putin posed hand-in-hand for pictures. Leaders from Iran and the United Arab Emirates met. And Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim even broke into a Bollywood number.

"The summit provided an opportunity for India to demonstrate its diversified portfolio of partnerships, to reiterate that it can be a voice of the Global South and venue for adversaries to communicate," said Tanvi Madan, senior fellow in the Foreign Policy program at the Brookings Institution.

"But there are tradeoffs involved, including bolstering a platform that enables China’s global influence," said Madan, adding that providing a stage for Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian and Putin has the potential to upset India’s other partners, which it would need to mitigate.

The summit may have been India's moment, but China's influence was evident in the agenda it advanced.

Xi said China would lead the creation of a BRICS AI Open Source Zone to promote cooperation on large language models. He also proposed a BRICS Special Economic Zone partnership and called for more stable industrial and supply chains across an integrated BRICS market. Read here for more on Xi's comments.

"If BRICS is a meeting of equals, China is the most equal," said Allen R. Carlson, an associate professor in Cornell University's government department, adding that China drove much of the agenda.

"Whatever is built from these proposals, it is hard to imagine the infrastructure coming from anywhere other than Beijing," Carlson said, while cautioning that "BRICS proposals tend to be more show than substance".

Read here about the evolution of BRICS and the challenges it faces today.

PAYMENTS AT THE CENTRE OF ECONOMIC AGENDA

The New Delhi summit of the BRICS bloc, now comprising 11 countries, according to the official BRICS website, came a quarter century after the idea was first proposed by former Goldman Sachs economist Jim O'Neill, who argued that a group of large emerging economies could steadily command a larger share of global growth and influence.

BRICS now accounts for about 28% of global GDP.

The bloc's growing economic weight was reflected in the communique, which renewed calls for emerging economies to wield greater influence in multilateral institutions like the International Monetary Fund.

BRICS leaders also backed further efforts to promote trade settlement and investment in local currencies and make central bank digital currencies (CBDCs) across these countries interoperable. Read here for more on that.

O'Neill himself believes this could be the new raison d'être for BRICS in the near future, he told Karin Strohecker of Reuters in an interview in July. Read his comments here.

While far less provocative than the idea of a common BRICS currency — which was never widely viewed as practical — encouraging trade in local currencies and linking payment systems are seen by many analysts as a more achievable objective.

Such initiatives are unlikely to challenge the dollar's dominant role in global finance. But they could lower transaction costs, reduce remittance expenses and provide alternatives during periods of geopolitical uncertainty, said Shashwat Alok, associate professor of finance at the Indian School of Business.

But questions over which country controls the architecture could cloud progress. For instance, a payment bridge platform for CBDCs called mBridge, anchored by China, prompted India to stay away. New Delhi recently stalled a proposal for a linkage of real-time payment systems between India and China-linked Alipay+.

"Settlement infrastructure is never neutral. Whoever runs the ledger and writes the membership rules holds a chokepoint. BRICS would do well to make sure that no one country has monopoly over the trade settlement architecture," Alok said.

MARKET MATTERS

The inflation rate in India rose to 4.82% in August, remaining above the central bank's 4% target and setting the stage for its first interest rate hike in nearly four years.

Economists pointed to signs of higher food and fuel prices pushing up costs across different categories.

The Reserve Bank of India laid the ground for tighter monetary policy last week when it chose to withdraw surplus liquidity from the banking sector via bond sales.

It will likely follow this up with a 25-basis-point hike in the policy repo rate in October and another similar-sized increase in December, Soumya Kanti Ghosh, chief economist at State Bank of India, said in a note.

THIS WEEK'S MUST-READS

Top reads this week come from across the corporate sector, with India's largest exchange set for an IPO and a large conglomerate being pushed towards listing.

Don't miss these stories:

  • Singapore Airlines to seek tougher terms for any fresh Air India funding, sources say

  • India's central bank rejects Tata Sons request to avoid public listing, sources say

  • India's NSE set to list in a long-delayed IPO

  • VinFast plans to develop two India-specific EVs in strategy shift, sources say

​

data.title: ZAWYA: Air Arabia-led consortium gets green light for new Saudi budget carrier in Dammam
data.description:
By Staff Writer

Saudi Arabia’s General Authority of Civil Aviation (GACA) has granted a consortium led by Air Arabia an Air Operator Certificate (AOC) to launch the Kingdom’s new national low-cost carrier, based at King Fahd International Airport in Dammam.

The certificate was issued in the presence of Minister of Transport and Logistic Services and GACA Chairman Saleh Al-Jasser, and GACA President Abdulaziz Al-Duailej, following the consortium’s successful completion of regulatory and operational requirements covering safety, security and operational quality.

The consortium, comprising Air Arabia Group, Nesma Group and KUN Holding Company, was selected by GACA in July 2025 as the winning bidder to establish and operate the new airline, with majority Saudi ownership.

The carrier is expected to create more than 2,400 direct jobs, contribute to GDP growth and strengthen tourism and air connectivity in Saudi Arabia’s Eastern Province, supporting the objectives of the Kingdom’s aviation programme.

Sulaiman Almuhaimedi, Executive Vice President of Aviation Safety and Environmental Sustainability at GACA, said that granting the AOC to the new carrier represents a significant step towards the Kingdom’s aviation strategy which aims to position Saudi Arabia as a global logistics hub and an international aviation hub.

He added: “The launch of Air Arabia’s operations from Dammam will contribute to enhancing competition and improving performance in the air transport market, while supporting trade and tourism in the Eastern Province and creating new local employment opportunities.”

He noted that the license was granted after the airline successfully completed all the required technical and regulatory stages and procedures to ensure the highest levels of safety and operational compliance. He further highlighted that this milestone reflects GACA’s role as the regulator of the air transport industry and its efforts to create an attractive investment environment.

He also noted that the new carrier will strengthen the Kingdom’s air connectivity by serving 24 domestic and 57 international destinations and is expected to carry approximately 10 million passengers annually by 2030, in line with the goals of the aviation programme.

data.title: HC Orders Review of 1, Other Extremely Low Defence Bids
data.description:
Manu Pubby New Delhi: In a ruling that can have far-reaching consequences for the defence industry, the Andhra Pradesh High Court has held that contracts cannot be mechanically awarded to the lowest bidder when the quoted price is so low that it raises doubts about the company's ability to deliver. Last week, the Andhra Pradesh High Court at Amaravati said that when a bid value is abnormally low, a viability assessment needs to be conducted before the contract is awarded.

The court ruling came in a case concerning the development-cum-production partnership (DCPP) model of the Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO), under which companies are invited to co-develop weapon technologies. Firms are initially invited to bid for a limited development order, typically covering a small number of prototypes.

The lowest-ranked bidders selected under the tender then work with DRDO to develop, test and demonstrate the system against the stipulated performance requirements. Once the equipment clears the required developmental and user trials and is found fit for operational induction, the armed forces can place larger production orders. Because the initial development phase is limited in quantity but carries high upfront costs, including engineering, trials and certification, companies may be willing to absorb part of the initial expenditure, or even incur losses, at that stage in the expectation of a larger follow-on order.

There have been instances in the past where abnormally low bids have been placed during DCPP competitions. In one particular case, a company even submitted a bid of one rupee to develop prototypes, resulting in it being selected as the DCPP winner for a weapon urgently needed by the armed forces. The Andhra HC ruling came in a petition filed by defence player Jaykay Enterprises regarding a DCPP project to develop the processor-based moored mine - next generation.

The company alleged that the winner of the contract, Apollo Micro Systems, had submitted an abnormally low bid that did not even cover the basic cost of materials required to manufacture the mines. In its judgement, the HC referred to a procedural failure on the part of DRDO, as it had not conducted a pre-award scrutiny for an abnormally low bid, as mandated under the DRDO Procurement Manual, 2025. It has asked the relevant authorities to conduct the scrutiny and proceed with the contract only if all conditions are met.

data.title: Code of Conduct Only for Smaller Cos?
data.description:
Tanya Pandey A call by Anthropic chief executive Dario Amodei to slow the pace of frontier artificial intelligence (AI) development has opened up a much wider debate over how fast the technology should advance. OpenAI chief executive Sam Altman, xAI chief Elon Musk, Microsoft chief Satya Nadella and even the United Nations human rights chief Volker Turk have since joined Dario to call for a pause, as concerns over AI safety meet questions around the cost of building frontier models, the loss of jobs, impact on the environment along with its use for autonomous and dangerous weapons.

But are the calls for pacing development genuinely about bringing in greater oversight or is a ploy for a cover up, Tanya Pandey explains. What are the calls for a slowdown, what do they comprise? The calls are not for stopping AI development. They are about giving safety testing and oversight more time to keep up with increasingly capable models, through independent evaluations, common safety standards, and greater coordination between companies and governments.

Why is it an issue now? AI systems are becoming more autonomous and are taking on tasks that previously required humans. They are also increasingly being used to write code and help develop other AI systems, raising concerns that capabilities could improve faster than companies can understand and control them. Former employees of some of these labs have come out in the open to express concerns and have even warned that AI could kill humans by end of this decade.

Could the slowdown also protect big AI labs? As Chinese open-weight models such as Kimi K3, DeepSeek, Alibaba's Qwen and Z.ai's GLM become increasingly capable at a fraction of the cost of leading US models, tighter government controls could make it harder for smaller companies and open source developers to compete with the biggest labs.

Some critics argue this could help the leading AI companies retain their advantage. How is the market reacting to the calls? The AI boom has created a huge investment chain around chips, data centres and computing infrastructure. Investors are now assessing what a slower pace of frontier AI development could mean for that spending. SoftBank fell as much as 13.2%, while Kioxia, SK Hynix, Samsung, TSMC and Tokyo Electron also declined.

Is the AI industry also facing an economic problem? The cost of training frontier models has risen massively. Training some of the largest models now costs hundreds of millions of dollars, with future frontier training runs expected to cross $1 billion. At the same time, open source models are becoming more capable and cheaper, raising questions over whether frontier labs can keep spending at this pace.

How does the AI slowdown tie into the US-China race? The argument is that the US should maintain its lead while putting safeguards around frontier development, alongside tighter controls on advanced AI technology going to China. Beijing has rejected that approach, with its Foreign Ministry saying that "fearmongering, confrontation and vicious competition" would disrupt global AI governance.

What do IPO plans tell us about AI industry's position? The slowdown debate comes as biggest AI labs face massive commercial expectations. OpenAI has pushed its IPO plans out of 2026, after reportedly eyeing a valuation of around $1 trillion. Anthropic is preparing for a potential IPO and is reportedly seeking a valuation of over $2 trillion.

data.title: Solar Acquires South African Explosives Co Omnia for $1.3b
data.description:
Our Bureau New Delhi: Nagpur-headquartered Solar Industries has acquired South Africa's Omnia Holdings for $1.3 billion in one of the largest outbound mergers and acquisitions deals in the defence sector.

Solar's wholly owned, step-down subsidiary Solar SA Investments Pty will acquire all outstanding shares of Johannesburg Stock Exchange-listed Omnia in an all-cash transaction, the company said in a stock exchange disclosure on Monday. The deal is expected to enable Solar Industries to establish a platform for commercial explosives and blasting solutions internationally. "The acquisition by Solar SA of Omnia will create an integrated global blasting platform that combines Omnia's vertically integrated manufacturing capabilities, ammonium nitrate production, surface bulk explosives and blasting services with Solar Group's leadership in explosives, initiating systems and advanced blasting technologies," said Manish Nuwal, managing director and chief executive officer, Solar Group.

Solar Industries will also be buying Omnia's integrated crop nutrition and biological solutions business. The Nagpur-headquartered company currently makes explosives for defence and industrial applications. Its explosives are used as propellants for missiles as well as in the mining industry. Solar has also diversified its manufacturing activities to include supplies of loitering munitions and counter-drone systems. "Together, the combined group will be positioned to offer integrated blasting solutions, creating meaningful competitive advantages through enhanced supply security, greater economies of scale, technology differentiation, access to key mining markets across Africa and other international geographies, and deeper customer engagement," Nuwal said.

Solar reported FY26 revenue of Rs 9,965 crore ($1.03 billion) and has an order book of Rs 11,000 crore ($1.1 billion) from the defence sector as per its website. Omnia is a diversified global group with complementary chemical and specialised businesses serving customers across the mining, agriculture and chemicals sectors.

It has a physical presence in 23 countries and serves customers in more than 40 through 70 distribution centres, employing 3,500 people worldwide. It posted FY26 revenue of $1.4 billion. Manufacturers of explosives for defence applications have been looking to expand business in the backdrop of increased spending and the government's focus on indigenisation. Apollo Micro Systems recently acquired explosives manufacturer Premier Explosives for Rs 2,500 crore, enabling it to expand trinitrotoluene (TNT) capacity.

data.title: SB Energy Could Raise Up to $500 Million in Japan as Part of U.S. Listing
data.description:
By Kosaku Narioka

SB Energy could raise up to $500 million in Japan as part of its planned listing in the U.S.

The SoftBank Group unit said Tuesday that the amount to be raised in Japan would be decided at a later date when the offering price is determined, expected between September 2026 and February 2027.

SB Energy, an AI infrastructure platform backed by SoftBank, registered for the initial public offering earlier this month. The company said it would trade on Nasdaq under the symbol SBE.

SB Energy is aiming to raise between $5 billion and $7 billion in the IPO, The Wall Street Journal has reported.

data.title: High Demand Turns Cart Wheels at Big Festive Bash
data.description:
Writankar Mukherjee & Sharmistha Mukherjee Kolkata|New Delhi: Consumer demand in India scaled a five-year high in the first phase of the festive season, lifting hopes of manufacturers across categories including home appliances, automobiles, apparel and footwear. Sales growth during the period spanning Onam, Rakshabandhan and Ganesh Chaturthi came despite several price increases, reflecting underlying consumer optimism.

Industry executives are hopeful the momentum will sustain till Navratri-Diwali, the country's largest consumption period. The latest demand upswing is broad-based across categories, according to executives. Online platforms, including quick commerce and food delivery services, also reported strong growth. Volume sales of refrigerators, air-conditioners and washing machines rose 12-15% year-on-year during the first phase, led by Onam, while value sales grew faster at 18-23% thanks to the price hikes, according to manufacturers.

Smaller towns in Maharashtra and Karnataka too reported robust sales growth since the weekend for Ganesh Chaturthi. "Onam gave us a very encouraging start, with good sell-out and healthy channel stocking. We are also seeing good growth around Ganesh Chaturthi, driven largely by volumes," said Sanjay Chitkara, director at LG Electronics, the country's largest white goods maker. Momentum is strong in large screen TVs, four-door refrigerators, large washing machines and ACs. Automakers, too, clocked record festive sales. Maruti Suzuki posted a 61% on-year rise in retail sales during Onam, despite the festival season being spread over fewer days this year.

data.title: Motherson to Invest 11,000cr in TN, Create 7,000 Jobs
data.description:
Our Bureau Chennai: Samvardhana Motherson, along with its European and UK-based joint venture companies, on Monday signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) with the Tamil Nadu government to invest approximately Rs 11,000 crore in the state, creating around 7,000 employment opportunities.

The MoU was signed and exchanged in London by Barrie Painter, global head-marketing and communications, Samvardhana Motherson International Group, and Deepak Jacob, managing director, Guidance, Tamil Nadu government, in the presence of chief minister C Joseph Vijay.

The MoU is the first major investment announcement after Vijay arrived in the UK capital as part of his visit to attract investments and expand partnerships in sectors including advanced manufacturing, electric vehicles, electronics and global capability centres. The proposed investment will cover design, engineering, manufacturing, assembly and logistics facilities in Tamil Nadu and will span the next five years. "The investment brings Motherson's global joint venture network, technical partners from Europe and the UK, and its international capabilities to Tamil Nadu, further strengthening the state's position as a preferred destination for advanced manufacturing and global partnerships," Guidance said in a post on X.

The news of the proposed investment comes after the Opposition attacked the ruling TVK over the visit to London. The AIADMK on Monday questioned the need for such an overseas trip at taxpayers' expense. The party pointed out that a company established in India in 1986 and headquartered in Noida was among the businesses involved, raising questions over the rationale for Vijay travelling to the UK for investment promotion. "A company established in India in 1986, HQ Noida @actorvijay travels all the way to UK at taxpayers money to attract investment," AIADMK spokesperson Kovai Sathyan said in a post on X.

Earlier, the DMK, too, hit out at the chief minister claiming that the purpose of his visit was to "attend the car race of his friend Ajith". "He said that he is going to receive investment from London. But everybody saw that he had gone to see the car race of his friend Ajith," DMK spokesperson TKS Elangovan said.

data.title: Coforge Appoints Egon Zehnder for Board Search
data.description:
Our Bureau Bengaluru: Coforge has appointed global executive search firm Egon Zehnder to identify a new chairman and two additional independent directors, following the board unrest with two exits last week of the mid-tier IT firm's chairman Om Prakash Bhatt and Nomination and Remuneration Committee (NRC) chair DK Singh.

The existing board spoke to analysts on Monday, headed by interim chairman Vivek Sharma, who said he will oversee the process to elect a permanent chair but he would not be a candidate for the role. Sharma has been appointed as the interim chairman until January 31, 2027. On September 8, Bhatt resigned with immediate effect, following concerns around an internal audit over the company's board evaluation process under his watch.

data.title: Aneka Tambang's Gold Margins Seen Recovering to Support 2H Earnings — Market Talk
data.description: Aneka Tambang's gold margins are expected to recover, with sustained nickel ore momentum supporting stronger second-half earnings, Nomura analyst Ahmad Maghfur Usman notes. Although 2Q gross margin slipped to 15.7% from 19.2% in 1Q as tighter domestic gold trading margins halved precious metals profit, the company's fiscal 2026 operational guidance is broadly in line with expectations. The bank lowers its target price to 5,300 rupiah from 6,100 rupiah to reflect tighter domestic gold trading margins and higher first-half finance costs. Nomura maintains its buy rating on the stock. Shares are up 0.9% at 3,220 rupiah. (venkat.pr@wsj.com)
